title: Hidden trails - secrets of the park
text: Most tourists stick to the same routes. Escape the crowds at Yangjiajie (Great Wall-like ridge with a fraction of the visitors), remote Laowuchang with sky-top terraced rice fields, the original Huangshizhai plateau, or the 5-6 km forest path from Bailong to Tianzi Mountain.

title: Getting around inside the park
text: The park covers 369 km2 - you cannot walk it all. The 65-yuan transport ticket includes free shuttle buses on upper and lower loops (every 5-15 minutes until ~18:00). Cable cars go to Huangshizhai (65 yuan), Yangjiajie (76 yuan) and Tianzi Mountain (72 yuan).

title: Monkeys in the park - rules of engagement
text: Rhesus macaques live throughout Zhangjiajie, especially along Golden Whip Stream. Never show food, do not smile (bared teeth signal aggression), avoid direct eye contact, never touch babies. If a monkey grabs your bag, let go - things are not worth a bite.

title: How the floating mountains of Zhangjiajie formed
text: The quartzite sandstone pillars are 380 million years old. Once a shallow sea, sediment compacted into stone, then tectonic uplift exposed it. Wind, water and tree roots slowly carved out cracks, leaving 3,000+ freestanding pillars up to 400 m tall - unique on Earth.

title: What to pack for Zhangjiajie park
text: Essentials: comfortable non-slip shoes (trails get wet), a raincoat (not umbrella - useless on narrow paths), 1.5-2 liters of water, power bank and sunscreen. Useful extras: gloves in winter, snacks, offline maps and motion sickness pills for bus serpentines.
